parameters.query:
-- Runs before any fetching. Seen before, has an email address, never sent.
-- One row out ({backlog: [...]}) so the fetch nodes after this still run once.
-- Company suppression still applies later, in Dedupe & Cap.
SELECT coalesce(json_agg(t), '[]'::json) AS backlog FROM (
  SELECT dedupe_key, source, company, title, city, country, region, url, contact_email
  FROM job_applications
  WHERE coalesce(contact_email, '') <> ''
    AND status IN ('dry_run', 'letter_failed', 'score_failed', 'rejected_fit', 'deferred')
  ORDER BY applied_at DESC
  LIMIT 50
) t;

assignments.name: showcaseFacts
assignments.value: n8n orchestration, models via OpenRouter (deepseek-v4-flash). Five public job sources: a 55-company Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby board registry, the Bundesagentur v6 API, Arbeitnow, Adzuna and Instaffo. Scans ~494 open engineering roles across Berlin, Bayern and Amsterdam each morning. Two-stage LLM: a cheap scoring pass gates the more expensive generation pass, cutting token spend several-fold and removing the bias of one call both writing and grading a letter. Postgres-backed dedupe with fuzzy title matching. The final submit stays manual on purpose: the ATS apply APIs all require the employer's own key.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO job_applications
  (dedupe_key, source, company, title, city, country, region, url,
   contact_email, fit, score_reason, lang, letter, channel, status)
SELECT d.dedupe_key, d.source, d.company, d.title, d.city, d.country, d.region, d.url,
       d.contact_email, d.fit, d.score_reason, d.lang, d.letter, d.channel, d.status
FROM jsonb_to_record($1::jsonb) AS d(
  dedupe_key text, source text, company text, title text, city text, country text,
  region text, url text, contact_email text, fit int, score_reason text, lang text,
  letter text, channel text, status text)
WHERE d.dedupe_key IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO UPDATE
  SET status = EXCLUDED.status, fit = EXCLUDED.fit, score_reason = EXCLUDED.score_reason,
      lang = EXCLUDED.lang, channel = EXCLUDED.channel,
      letter = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.letter, job_applications.letter),
      contact_email = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.contact_email, job_applications.contact_email),
      applied_at = now();

parameters.jsCode:
const cfg = $('Config1').first().json;
// All targets at once: Generate Outreach then runs the requests concurrently.
return $input.all().map(({ json: j }) => {
  const german = /\.(de|at)$/.test(j.domain || '') || (j.regions || []).some(r => r === 'bayern' || r === 'berlin');
  const lang = german ? 'German' : 'English';

  const sys = [
    'You write a speculative job application (Initiativbewerbung) from a software engineer.',
    'Return STRICT JSON only: {"subject":"...","body":"..."}',
    'Write subject and body in ' + lang + '.',
    'There is NO specific open role. Do not invent one or claim to have seen a posting.',
    'Write in first person as the candidate. Never mention how this role or company was found, and never say or imply that this text was written, drafted or sent by a tool, pipeline, agent or automation.',
    'First paragraph: who the candidate is (from the CV) and why they are writing to THIS company.',
    'Second paragraph: the one or two CV projects most relevant to what this company hires for.',
    'Name one concrete engineering decision from them and why it was made, using only what the CV',
    'states. A build description, not a feature list.',
    'Third paragraph: ask whether an engineering opening that fits the CV (AI/ML, full-stack, backend',
    'or frontend - whichever matches what they hire for) exists or is planned. One clear, low-pressure ask.',
    (j.tier === 'general'
      ? 'This address is a GENERAL company inbox, not a recruiting one. Open with a single short '
        + 'polite line asking whoever reads it to forward the mail to whoever handles engineering '
        + 'hiring, then continue. Keep it brief and do not apologise at length.'
      : j.tier === 'people'
        ? 'This address reaches HR/People directly. Address them as such; no forwarding request needed.'
        : 'This is a dedicated recruiting address. Write straight to the hiring team.'),
    'HARD RULE: no claim of experience, tools or results absent from the CV.',
    'Tone: engineer to engineer. No hype, no "passionate", no "excited", no superlatives.',
    'COMPANY-SPECIFIC, MANDATORY: use the COMPANY BRIEF below. Reference something concrete and true',
    'of this company - the disciplines they are hiring into, tech recurring in their own ad titles,',
    'or how they describe themselves. Two mails to two companies must share no sentence.',
    'Never use wording that would fit any employer ("innovative", "market leader", "exciting work").',
    'If the brief is thin, write less rather than padding. Do not invent products, funding,',
    'customers or headcount the brief does not state.',
    'body: 200-280 words, plain text, no markdown.',
    cfg.portfolioUrl
      ? 'Sign off with name, phone, LinkedIn and the write-up link ' + cfg.portfolioUrl
      : 'Sign off with name, phone and LinkedIn. Do NOT include any URL, repository or portfolio '
        + 'link anywhere - none exists. Do not invent one and do not offer to send one.',
    'Say a CV is attached.'
  ].join(' ');

  const usr = ['CV:', cfg.cvText, '',
    'CONTACT: ' + cfg.myName + ', ' + cfg.myPhone + ', ' + cfg.myEmail + ', ' + cfg.myLinkedIn, '',
    'COMPANY: ' + j.name + '  (' + j.domain + ')',
    'Regions where they hire engineers: ' + (j.regions || []).join(', '), '',
    'COMPANY BRIEF (only permitted source for claims about them):',
    j.companyBrief || '(no detail retrieved - keep it short and do not speculate)'].join('\n');

  return { json: { ...j, lang, llmPayload: {
    model: cfg.letterModel,
    messages: [{ role: 'system', content: sys }, { role: 'user', content: usr }],
    max_tokens: 6000,
    temperature: Number(cfg.letterTemperature ?? 0.4),
    reasoning: { effort: cfg.letterEffort || 'low' },
    response_format: { type: 'json_object' } } } };
});

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO employer_candidates (name, norm_name, regions, sources, ads)
SELECT c.name, c.norm_name, c.regions, c.sources, c.ads
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb)
  AS c(name text, norm_name text, regions text[], sources text[], ads int)
ON CONFLICT (norm_name) DO UPDATE SET
  last_seen = now(), seen_count = employer_candidates.seen_count + 1,
  ads = GREATEST(employer_candidates.ads, EXCLUDED.ads),
  regions = ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT unnest(employer_candidates.regions || EXCLUDED.regions)),
  sources = ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT unnest(employer_candidates.sources || EXCLUDED.sources));
SELECT name, ats, token, regions, options FROM employers WHERE active;

INSERT INTO job_applications
  (dedupe_key, source, company, title, city, country, region, url,
   contact_email, fit, score_reason, lang, letter, channel, status)
SELECT d.dedupe_key, d.source, d.company, d.title, d.city, d.country, d.region, d.url,
       d.contact_email, d.fit, d.score_reason, d.lang, d.letter, d.channel, d.status
FROM jsonb_to_record($1::jsonb) AS d(
  dedupe_key text, source text, company text, title text, city text, country text,
  region text, url text, contact_email text, fit int, score_reason text, lang text,
  letter text, channel text, status text)
WHERE d.dedupe_key IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO UPDATE
  SET status = EXCLUDED.status, fit = EXCLUDED.fit, score_reason = EXCLUDED.score_reason,
      lang = EXCLUDED.lang, channel = EXCLUDED.channel,

nodes.name: Generate Letter

parameters.jsCode:
const cfg = $('Config').first().json;
// All passers at once: Generate Letter then runs the requests concurrently.
return $input.all().map(({ json: j }) => {
  const desc = String(j.description || '');
  const germanish = /(wir suchen|deine aufgaben|ihre aufgaben|abgeschlossenes|kenntnisse|unbefristet|m\/w\/d|bewerbung)/i.test(desc);
  const englishish = /(you will|your profile|we offer|responsibilities|requirements)/i.test(desc);
  const lang = j.country === 'NL' ? 'English' : (germanish && !englishish ? 'German' : 'English');
  // Moving to Amsterdam (2026-11-18): Dutch letters say so once, so nobody wonders about a candidate in Nuremberg.
  const reloc = j.country === 'NL' && cfg.relocationNoteNL ? String(cfg.relocationNoteNL) : '';

  const sys = [
    'You are ' + cfg.myName + '. You have just read the job posting below, you want this job, and you',
    'are writing your own cover letter for it. Everything you know about yourself is in the CV.',
    '',
    'BEFORE WRITING, work through this silently (do not output it):',
    '1. The job: what does this team build, what problem is this hire meant to solve, and which 3-4',
    '   requirements matter most? Ignore boilerplate (benefits, generic "team player" lines).',
    '2. The match: for each of those requirements, find the closest thing in the CV.',
    '   - Direct match: the specific project or role, and what you actually did there.',
    '   - Partial match: the nearest related experience and exactly how it carries over (same kind',
    '     of problem, similar stack, same domain).',
    '   - No match: leave it out, or give it one confident sentence on how you would close it.',
    '3. The angle: the single strongest reason you are a good hire for THIS role. Build the letter',
    '   around it. Present yourself in the terms of the role (a backend engineer for a backend role,',
    '   a frontend engineer for a frontend role, an ML engineer for an ML role), using the parts of',
    '   the CV that fit. The CV covers AI/LLM, full-stack, backend, frontend, mobile and data work.',
    '',
    'THE LETTER (field "body"):',
    '- Greeting. ' + (lang === 'German'
      ? 'German: formal "Sie". "Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren," unless the posting names a contact person.'
      : 'English: "Dear ' + j.company + ' team," unless the posting names a contact person.'),
    '- Opening, 2-3 sentences: name the role, say what specifically about this team, product or',
    '  problem makes you want it (something concrete from the posting), and who you are in one line.',
    '- Middle, one or two paragraphs: your 2-3 strongest matches, each a concrete example from the CV',
    '  - what you built, a decision you made and why - tied to a requirement the posting names.',
    '  Weave any bridging into these examples; never write a list of what you lack.',
    '- Close, 2-3 sentences: what you would take on first, given what the posting says the team',
    '  needs, and a simple ask for a conversation. Mention that your CV is attached.',
    ...(reloc ? ['- Relocation: in the close, one sentence in your own words saying: "' + reloc + '" This is the',
      '  only exception to the rule on visa and nationality below.'] : []),
    '- Sign-off with name, phone and LinkedIn.',
    '- 200-280 words. Plain text, no markdown, no bullet points. Write in ' + lang + '.',
    '',
    'VOICE: first person, direct, an engineer writing to engineers. Concrete nouns over adjectives.',
    'Vary sentence length. Confident, never apologetic. Banned: "I am writing to apply",',
    '"passionate", "excited", "dynamic", "team player", "great fit", "hit the ground running",',
    '"leverage", "innovative", "market leader", "exciting projects", "I believe I would".',
    'Every paragraph must contain something true of THIS company and posting, so that the letter',
    'would make no sense if sent to another company. If the posting is thin, write less rather',
    'than padding.',
    '',
    'NEVER INCLUDE: salary or salary expectations, notice period or Kuendigungsfrist, start date or',
    'Eintrittstermin, visa or nationality, how you found the job, any mention of a tool, pipeline or',
    'automation writing or sending this letter, any fit score, or any placeholder like [Name].',
    '',
    'TRUTH: every fact about you must come from the CV - no invented employers, projects, years,',
    'tools, certifications or numbers. Adapt emphasis and framing freely; never the facts.',
    '',
    'Return STRICT JSON only, with exactly these fields:',
    '{"subject":"...","body":"...","talkingPoints":["..."],"linkedinNote":"...","angle":"..."}',
    'subject: in ' + lang + ', "Application: <exact job title>" (German: "Bewerbung als <Titel>").',
    'talkingPoints: 2-3 items in English, each "CV project -> requirement from the posting".',
    'linkedinNote: max 300 characters, sent by hand to an engineer or hiring lead at the company:',
    'one line on the role, one concrete hook from the CV, one short ask. No greeting padding, no',
    'hashtags. English unless the posting is German.',
    'angle: one English sentence - the strongest reason you fit this role.'
  ].join('\n');

  const usr = ['CV:', cfg.cvText, '',
    'CONTACT: ' + cfg.myName + ', ' + cfg.myPhone + ', ' + cfg.myEmail + ', ' + cfg.myLinkedIn, '',
    'JOB: ' + j.title + ' at ' + j.company + ' (' + [j.city, j.country].filter(Boolean).join(', ') + ')',
    'Link: ' + j.url, '',
    'Where the CV is thinnest for this role, from screening (bridge these, never list them): '
      + ((j.missing || []).join('; ') || 'nothing flagged'), '',
    'POSTING:', desc.slice(0, 6000) || '(no description available - keep the letter short and do not guess details)'
  ].join('\n');

  return { json: { ...j, lang, llmPayload: {
    model: cfg.letterModel,
    messages: [{ role: 'system', content: sys }, { role: 'user', content: usr }],
    // Reasoning models spend part of this on thinking; 2500 left v4.1-flash with no answer.
    max_tokens: 6000,
    temperature: Number(cfg.letterTemperature ?? 0.4),
    reasoning: { effort: cfg.letterEffort || 'low' },
    response_format: { type: 'json_object' } } } };
});

parameters.query:
-- Every open apply-yourself job (this run's included - Save Application ran first), newest first.
SELECT dedupe_key, company, title, city, region, url, contact_email, fit, score_reason, letter, status,
       to_char(applied_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS added
FROM job_applications
WHERE status IN ('manual', 'send_failed')
  AND applied_at > now() - make_interval(days => $1::int)
ORDER BY applied_at DESC
LIMIT 1000;
